key_insight: A tool-calling ReAct LLM can turn natural-language home energy requests into near-optimal appliance schedules, but only when its outputs are validated before execution.
engineering_relevance: For HEMS deployment, the main value is flexible orchestration across dynamic tariffs, weather, PV forecasts, and user preferences without requiring technical constraint encoding.
method: Evaluated five LLM backends on multi-appliance scheduling tasks
Compared native function calling vs text-parsed actions against a MILP benchmark
Tested tariff changes, constraint conflicts, weather-aware scheduling, and a 7-day rolling deployment
evidence_signal: Across a seven-day period, the agents captured 96.7–98.0% of the savings available between an off-peak timer and the MILP oracle and outperformed rule-based policies.
watch_item: LLM schedules can be fabricated or infeasible, so every committed plan should pass an independent deterministic feasibility check before actuation.
paper_title: LLMs for Agentic Home Energy Management
